chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Sleeping, eating, drinking and gambling on the road
summary: The band slept in beds four or five nights a week, ate cold cuts, barely drank, knew no marijuana until about 1939, and only two gambled.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I am simply amazed that you were able to play well when you must have been tired all the time. How many nights in a week did you sleep in a bed as opposed to sleeping in the car...?
When we was on the road, playing the one-nighters, we'd sleep about four or five nights a week.
In a bed.
Yeah..
That wouldn't be too bad.
No.
But I mean, you'd still be two or three nights sitting up
Buster Smith - 41
all the time.
Oh yeah.
And what about food? Did you look after yourselves properly? Did you eat properly? Or did you just grab anything that you could get...?

No, we'd stop on the road in little groceries, drive-ins and things, pick up little sandwiches and whatnot, little cold-cuts. What the boys called cold-cuts -- sardines and stuff like that. Black ham.
Was there a lot of drinking in the band?
No. Not the Blue Devils, no. Didn't drink much. No, it was just two or three of them really.
What about smoking stuff? Were any of the guys taking marijuana?
No, no. They didn't know about nothin' like that in them days.
Really?
No. Never heard of it. Never heard of nothin' like that.
That was more of a New York thing.
Yeah. You had that stuff way up in the thirties. Yeah. About '39.
Was it a gambling band?
No.
Buster Smith - 42
Any of the guys sort of play..
Yeah, we had one or two...about three of them. We had the bass player.
Alvin Burroughs, isn't it? [HE WAS THE DRUMMER]
(?)Alvin Burroughs(?). He loved to shoot dice. Charlie Washington also loved to shoot dice. Now, them's the two that would gamble. But all the rest of these boys, they wouldn't gaamble.
